text.p: Following are some of the main
stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified
these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- The Amsterdam stock exchange closed earlier on Friday as a
result of the more than four percent plunge of the AEX-index.
- Employers association VNO-NCW worried about workers union
FNV's four to five percent wage demand for next year. (p1)
- Court rules that the traffic minister and not Schiphol
Airport is authorized to impose a ban on night flights. (p1)
- Light bulb makers Philips and Osram are sceptical about
General Electric's plans to conquer 25 pct of the Dutch market.
- Volume of trade by private investors on the Amsterdam
stock exchange doubled in 1996 in money terms, compared with the
previous year. (p15)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Measures to fight aeroplane noise at Schiphol Airport come
too late to have effect this year. (p1)
- Computer shops chain Commodore it to institute insolvency
procedures. (p2)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Employers association VNO-NCW and workers unions FNV and
CNV are working on a plan for keeping their say in pension
schemes. (p11)
- Bourse management is not expecting a Black Monday
following New York stock exchange's nosedive on Friday. (p11)
TROUW
- Security analyst G. Panjer expects the Amsterdam stock
exchange to follow that of New York with about five percent drop
in share prices. (p3)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Parties in parliament support fiscal plans of finance
minister Gerrit Zalm and junior finance minister Wim Vermeend.
